lessons.title: Number and Place Value 1
lessons.description:
In this video, students will learn how numbers build up to 1000 and beyond.
We will use visual models and place value charts to explore thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones.

Students will also:
✔ Represent thousands using visual models
✔ Partition numbers in standard and non-standard ways
✔ Break 1000 into equal parts
✔ Compare, order, and compose four-digit numbers
✔ Solve word problems using partitioning

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently represent and partition large numbers.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Number and Place Value 2
lessons.description:
In this video, students will build on their knowledge of partitioning and place value.
They will represent and break apart four-digit numbers and write them in expanded form.

Students will also:
✔ Partition four-digit numbers using place value models
✔ Solve word problems using partitioning
✔ Explore number lines and currency examples
✔ Find 1000 more or 1000 less
✔ Play games to apply these skills

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently represent and manipulate four-digit numbers.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Number and Place Value 3
lessons.description:
In this video, students will learn how to compare and round four-digit numbers.
They will use place value to compare, order, and estimate numbers.

Students will also:
✔ Check comparison statements using place value reasoning
✔ Order numbers accurately
✔ Place numbers on number lines
✔ Round numbers to the nearest ten

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently compare, order, and round four-digit numbers.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Number and Place Value 4
lessons.description:
In this video, students will explore negative numbers in real-life contexts.
They will count below zero and read temperatures using negative values.

Students will also:
✔ Understand negative numbers and zero
✔ Fill in missing numbers on number lines
✔ Read temperatures on thermometers
✔ Solve real-life temperature problems

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently use negative numbers.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Number and Place Value 5
lessons.description:
In this video, students will explore negative numbers in real-life contexts.
They will count below zero and read temperatures using negative values.

Students will also:
✔ Understand negative numbers and zero
✔ Fill in missing numbers on number lines
✔ Read temperatures on thermometers
✔ Solve real-life temperature problems

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently use negative numbers.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Number and Place Value 6
lessons.description:
In this video, students will explore negative numbers in real-life contexts.
They will count below zero and read temperatures using negative values.

Students will also:
✔ Understand negative numbers and zero
✔ Fill in missing numbers on number lines
✔ Read temperatures on thermometers
✔ Solve real-life temperature problems

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently use negative numbers.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Addition
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn four-digit column addition step by step.
They start with simple additions and move on to regrouping and trickier problems.

Students will practise:
✔ Basic addition facts
✔ Using place value to add large numbers
✔ Regrouping correctly
✔ Solving missing digit problems
✔ Fun challenge activities
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Subtraction
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn how to subtract four-digit numbers using the column method.
They start with simple calculations and move on to exchanges.

This lesson includes:
✔ Subtraction with and without exchanges
✔ Place value models for understanding
✔ Fun puzzles and challenges
✔ Real-life examples
✔ Efficient subtraction strategies

By the end of the lesson, learners will be confident with column subtraction.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Addition and Subtraction
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students explore addition and subtraction problem-solving using real-life examples.
They learn how to choose the correct operation and check answers using the inverse.

This lesson includes:
✔ Two-step word problems
✔ Addition and subtraction keyword activities
✔ Real-life examples
✔ Checking answers using inverse operations
✔ Practice challenges
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Rule of 3
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn the Rule of Three to solve proportion problems.
They practise cross multiplication and division using real-life examples.

This lesson includes:
✔ Understanding proportions
✔ Step-by-step Rule of Three method
✔ Real-life word problems
✔ Measurement conversions
✔ Practice worksheets
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Converting Lengths
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn how to convert between different units of length.
They practise converting and comparing measurements.

This lesson includes:
✔ Ordering units of length
✔ Converting between mm, cm, m, and km
✔ Real-life examples
✔ Solving word problems
✔ Comparing and ordering measurements
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Comparing and Calculating Lengths
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn how to compare and order lengths.
They convert between centimetres, metres, and kilometres to solve problems.

This lesson includes:
✔ Converting units of length
✔ Comparing and ordering measurements
✔ Real-life word problems
✔ Fun comparison challenges
✔ Subtraction problems with distances
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Area
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students explore the concept of area.
They learn how to measure the space inside shapes using unit squares and multiplication.

This lesson includes:
✔ Understanding area in real life
✔ Counting squares to find area
✔ Using multiplication for rectangles
✔ Working with half-squares and composite shapes
✔ Practice activities
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Fractions 1
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students build a strong understanding of fractions.
They explore wholes, equal parts, and fractions greater than one using models and number lines.

This lesson includes:
✔ Identifying wholes and equal parts
✔ Unit and non-unit fractions
✔ Completing fractions to make a whole
✔ Counting in fractions on number lines
✔ Improper fractions and mixed numbers
✔ Step-by-step practice questions
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Fractions 2
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn about mixed numbers and how to represent, compare, and order fractions.
They use number lines and visual models to build confidence.

This lesson includes:
✔ Counting in fractional steps
✔ Writing mixed numbers from models
✔ Placing fractions on number lines
✔ Comparing and ordering mixed numbers
✔ Practice activities
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Fractions 3
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students explore improper fractions and mixed numbers.
They learn how to recognise, represent, and convert between them.

This lesson includes:
✔ Identifying improper fractions
✔ Using visual models and number lines
✔ Converting mixed numbers and improper fractions
✔ Times-table reasoning
✔ Guided practice and challenges
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Fractions 4
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn how to add and subtract fractions with the same denominator.
They also work with mixed numbers and improper fractions.

This lesson includes:
✔ Adding fractions with the same denominator
✔ Using models to visualise calculations
✔ Adding fractions to mixed numbers
✔ Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers
✔ Converting improper fractions to mixed numbers
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Fractions 5
lessons.description: Fractions 5: decimals, tenths, hundredths and partitioning.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Fractions 6
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students explore decimal halves and quarters.
They learn about equivalent fractions and rounding decimals.

This lesson includes:
✔ Equivalent fractions for halves and quarters
✔ Writing halves and quarters as decimals
✔ Using models and number lines
✔ Rounding decimals to the nearest whole
✔ Applying place value reasoning
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Fractions 7
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students compare and order decimal numbers.
They use place value knowledge and number lines to decide which decimals are greater or smaller.

This lesson includes:
✔ Linking fractions to decimals
✔ Comparing decimals using place value
✔ Using greater than, less than, and equals symbols
✔ Ordering decimals in ascending and descending order
✔ Solving mixed comparison problems
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Multiplication and Division
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students develop their multiplication and division skills by exploring multiples of 3, multiplying and dividing by 6, and multiplying and dividing by 9.

Students begin by learning the three times table using groups, repeated addition and number lines.

Students will:
✔ Count in multiples of 3
✔ Use repeated addition to represent multiplication
✔ Link groups of objects to multiplication calculations
✔ Recognise patterns in the three times table
✔ Use number lines to calculate multiples of 3

The lesson then explores how known multiplication facts can help solve larger calculations.
Students learn to build on known facts such as twelve times three to calculate more challenging multiples.

Students will also:
✔ Use known facts to solve larger calculations
✔ Count on in equal groups
✔ Explain multiplication patterns
✔ Apply efficient mental maths strategies

Next, students investigate multiples of 3 using digit sums.
They learn that if the sum of the digits is a multiple of 3, then the whole number is also a multiple of 3.

Students will:
✔ Find digit sums
✔ Test whether numbers are multiples of 3
✔ Identify multiples in large numbers
✔ Use divisibility rules confidently

The lesson then moves on to multiplying and dividing by 6.
Students use groups, sharing, grouping and arrays to explore multiplication and division facts.

Students will also:
✔ Represent multiplication using equal groups
✔ Use arrays to show rows and columns
✔ Understand that multiplication is commutative
✔ Divide by sharing equally
✔ Divide by grouping
✔ Write multiplication and division calculations from arrays

Students then explore fact families.
They learn how multiplication and division facts are linked together.

Students will:
✔ Create multiplication and division fact families
✔ Use arrays to identify related facts
✔ Correct mistakes in fact families
✔ Understand the relationship between multiplication and division

The lesson also shows how the six times table links to the three times table.
Students learn that multiplying by 6 can be found by doubling the answers in the three times table.

Students practise:
✔ Doubling multiples of 3
✔ Building fluency in the six times table
✔ Splitting numbers to solve larger multiplications
✔ Using partitioning strategies

Next, students move on to multiplying and dividing by 9.
They explore equal groups, arrays and fact families involving multiples of 9.

Students will also:
✔ Count in multiples of 9
✔ Use repeated addition with groups of 9
✔ Represent multiplication using arrays
✔ Solve division calculations by grouping
✔ Create fact families for the nine times table

Finally, students learn efficient strategies for calculating larger multiples of 9.
They use partitioning and known facts such as ten times nine to solve more challenging calculations.

Students will:
✔ Split numbers into easier parts
✔ Use known multiplication facts
✔ Add and subtract multiples efficiently
✔ Solve larger multiplication calculations mentally

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently identify multiples of 3 and use multiplication and division facts for 6 and 9 to solve a wide range of calculations.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Estimate, Compare & Calculate Money
lessons.description:
Today’s lesson lays the foundation for working with money in the real world.

In this video, students will learn how to estimate with money.
We will explore how to round amounts to the nearest pound, use number lines to check, and decide when to round up or down.
Students will practise adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing money in real-life shopping situations, and finding change quickly and accurately.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to:
✔ Estimate totals confidently
✔ Round prices to make calculations easier
✔ Work out exact costs and share amounts fairly
✔ Use quick methods to calculate change

This lesson builds strong money skills, boosts confidence with mental maths, and prepares students for everyday problem-solving.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Money 1
lessons.description:
In this video, students will learn all about pounds and pence.
We will explore how to identify, count, and combine coins and notes, and practise writing money amounts in different ways using words, pence, and decimal notation.

Students will also:
✔ Learn how pounds and pence link with decimals
✔ Practise comparing and ordering money amounts
✔ Convert between pence and pounds to make calculations easier
✔ Work with ascending and descending order of money values

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to count, compare, and convert money amounts with confidence.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Money 2
lessons.description:
In this video, students will learn how to estimate and work with money more confidently.
We will practise rounding amounts to the nearest pound, using number lines, and applying the tenths digit rule to decide whether to round up or down.

Students will also:
✔ Estimate totals and check if shop prices seem reasonable
✔ Add and subtract money using different strategies
✔ Work out change by counting up or using rounding shortcuts
✔ Handle tricky prices ending in .99 by rounding and adjusting accurately

By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to round, add, subtract, and estimate money totals quickly and correctly.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Money 3
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students explore money word problems using pounds and pence.
They practise adding costs, multiplying to find totals, and dividing amounts equally between people.

This lesson includes:
✔ Adding prices of different items
✔ Using multiplication to find costs of multiples
✔ Comparing costs
✔ Sharing the cost of items equally
✔ Step-by-step worked examples

Perfect for building confidence in solving real-life money problems.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Time 1
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn about years, months, weeks and days, and how these units of time are connected. They practise naming and ordering the months of the year, recalling how many days are in each month, identifying leap years, and converting between years and months. They also learn to use calendars to answer date questions and convert between weeks and days in real-life contexts.

This lesson includes:
✔ Ordering months and recalling the number of days in each month
✔ Understanding years, months, calendars, weeks and days
✔ Identifying leap years and explaining why February can have 29 days
✔ Converting between years and months
✔ Converting between weeks and days
✔ Solving mixed-unit problems with years and months or weeks and days
✔ Reading calendars to find dates and days of the week
✔ Using times tables and division facts to solve time problems
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Time 2
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn to convert between hours and minutes, and between minutes and seconds. They use the fact that there are 60 minutes in one hour and 60 seconds in one minute to solve conversions, compare durations, and work out mixed-unit time problems. They also apply these skills to real-life reasoning questions involving schedules, reading challenges and elapsed time.

This lesson includes:
✔ Converting hours to minutes and minutes to hours
✔ Converting minutes to seconds and seconds to minutes
✔ Solving mixed-unit problems such as hours and minutes, or minutes and seconds
✔ Comparing durations using greater than, less than and equals
✔ Using multiplication and division facts with 60
✔ Solving elapsed-time problems in real-life contexts
✔ Ordering times from shortest to longest
✔ Interpreting and solving reasoning problems with time tables and totals
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Time 3
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn how to convert between analogue clocks and twelve-hour digital times, and how to interpret and use the 24-hour clock. They practise reading minutes past and minutes to the hour, using a.m. and p.m. correctly, and converting times between 12-hour and 24-hour formats. They also solve elapsed-time problems involving start times and finish times.

This lesson includes:
✔ Reading analogue clocks and matching them to digital times
✔ Understanding minutes past and minutes to the hour
✔ Using a.m. and p.m. correctly
✔ Converting analogue times to 12-hour digital times
✔ Converting 12-hour times to 24-hour clock times
✔ Knowing when to add 12 for p.m. times after noon
✔ Solving start-time and finish-time problems
✔ Explaining and correcting common mistakes in time conversion
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Time 4
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students learn how to convert from 24-hour clock to 12-hour digital and analogue times. They practise identifying whether a 24-hour time is a.m. or p.m., subtracting 12 from times after noon, and matching 24-hour times to correct analogue clock faces. They also solve reasoning problems involving equivalent times and common conversion errors.

This lesson includes:
✔ Converting from 24-hour clock to 12-hour digital times
✔ Identifying whether a 24-hour time is a.m. or p.m.
✔ Subtracting 12 from times after 12:59 to convert to p.m. times
✔ Matching 24-hour times to analogue clocks
✔ Converting activities and schedules between time formats
✔ Explaining common mistakes in 24-hour to 12-hour conversion
✔ Recognising equivalent analogue, 12-hour and 24-hour times
✔ Solving reasoning problems using different clock representations
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Statistics 1
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students are introduced to statistics and learn how to collect, interpret and present discrete data.

In this video, students will learn what discrete data is.
They will understand that discrete data is counted and cannot have in-between values, such as the number of cars or children.

Students will begin with a real-life investigation, analysing different coloured cars passing a school. They will:
✔ Identify the most common category
✔ Compare values between categories
✔ Calculate totals

The lesson then introduces pictograms.
Students will learn that pictograms use symbols to represent data and that a key is essential.

Students will also:
✔ Interpret pictograms using a key
✔ Work out totals from symbols
✔ Compare categories
✔ Understand that symbols can represent more than one unit
✔ Use parts of symbols for smaller values

Next, students will learn how to draw pictograms.
They will:
✔ Choose an appropriate key
✔ Represent data accurately
✔ Use fractions of symbols where needed

The lesson then introduces bar charts.
Students will learn that bar charts:
✔ Have a horizontal axis for categories
✔ Have a vertical axis for values
✔ Use a number scale
✔ Include titles and labelled axes
✔ Have equal-width bars with gaps

Students will also:
✔ Read values from scales
✔ Compare categories
✔ Calculate differences and totals
✔ Choose appropriate scales such as 1, 2, 5 or 10

The lesson then extends to more advanced bar charts.

Grouped bar charts:
✔ Compare subcategories such as boys and girls
✔ Use multiple bars per category
✔ Require a key or legend

Stacked bar charts:
✔ Combine subcategories into one bar
✔ Help compare totals and parts together

Students will apply their learning to real datasets, such as birthdays across months.
They will interpret data, compare values, and answer questions.

The lesson then introduces Venn diagrams.
Students will learn that:
✔ Each circle represents a set
✔ Overlapping sections show shared data
✔ Items in overlaps belong to multiple categories

Students will also interpret Venn diagrams by:
✔ Identifying where data belongs
✔ Answering questions about combinations
✔ Understanding multiple overlaps with three sets

Finally, students are introduced to Carroll diagrams as another way to organise data into categories.

By the end of the lesson, learners will understand how to present and interpret data using different methods and use this knowledge to answer comparison and total-based questions.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Statistics 2
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students build on their understanding of statistics by interpreting and drawing bar charts and time graphs using both discrete and continuous data.

Students begin by using timelines and bar charts to investigate kings and queens from history.
They will:
✔ Read timelines accurately
✔ Match years to positions on a scale
✔ Interpret bar charts
✔ Compare lengths of reigns
✔ Calculate totals and differences from charts

The lesson then introduces grouped bar charts.
Students learn that grouped bar charts compare two sets of related data using a key or legend.

Students will also:
✔ Compare two pieces of information side by side
✔ Interpret grouped bar charts
✔ Identify similarities and differences in data
✔ Answer reasoning questions using scales and bars

Next, students explore countryside statistics using tally charts and frequency tables.
They will:
✔ Count tally marks in groups of five
✔ Complete missing frequencies
✔ Interpret discrete data
✔ Calculate totals and differences
✔ Identify the highest and lowest frequencies

Students then move on to drawing and interpreting bar charts.
They learn that bar charts:
✔ Use horizontal and vertical axes
✔ Need a suitable scale
✔ Must include labels and titles
✔ Require equal-width bars with gaps between them

Students will also:
✔ Spot mistakes in incorrect bar charts
✔ Compare categories visually
✔ Solve reasoning problems using data
✔ Interpret scales accurately

The lesson then introduces continuous data and time graphs.
Students learn that continuous data is measured and can have in-between values.

Students will:
✔ Understand the difference between discrete and continuous data
✔ Read and interpret time graphs
✔ Measure distance against time
✔ Estimate values between plotted points
✔ Calculate changes over time

Students also learn how to:
✔ Read scales carefully
✔ Follow points across axes
✔ Find approximate values from graphs
✔ Compare distances and times

The lesson then explores true and false reasoning questions using bar charts.
Students will:
✔ Evaluate statements using data
✔ Calculate totals and differences
✔ Explain whether statements are true or false

Next, students investigate temperatures using thermometers, bar charts and time graphs.
They will:
✔ Read temperatures in degrees Celsius
✔ Record continuous data
✔ Compare temperatures across days
✔ Calculate temperature differences
✔ Decide which graph type is most appropriate

Students then compare temperatures from different cities around the world.
They will:
✔ Interpret bar charts showing city temperatures
✔ Compare values between cities
✔ Identify equal and greater values
✔ Answer multi-step comparison questions

Finally, students are introduced to double time graphs.
They learn that double time graphs compare two sets of continuous data over the same time period.

Students will also:
✔ Compare two lines on one graph
✔ Calculate differences between datasets
✔ Interpret changes over time visually
✔ Analyse patterns and trends

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently interpret and compare data using timelines, tally charts, grouped bar charts, bar charts, time graphs and double time graphs.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Statistics 3
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students continue developing their statistics skills by interpreting and drawing bar charts, line graphs and time graphs using real-life data.

Students begin with gardening statistics.
They measure sunflower heights using a metre stick and record the data in a table.

Students will:
✔ Read scales accurately
✔ Measure heights in centimetres
✔ Complete data tables
✔ Compare values
✔ Calculate differences and totals

The lesson then explores which type of graph is most suitable for presenting data.
Students learn that:
✔ Bar charts are useful for comparing categories
✔ Time graphs are used when data changes over time
✔ Discrete data uses separate categories
✔ Continuous data is measured over time

Students then interpret bar charts by:
✔ Identifying the tallest and shortest values
✔ Calculating differences between categories
✔ Finding combined totals
✔ Solving reasoning questions using graph data

Next, students investigate runner bean growth over two weeks.
They learn how to present continuous data using a time graph.

Students will also:
✔ Understand how time graphs show change over time
✔ Read horizontal and vertical axes
✔ Choose suitable scales
✔ Plot and join points correctly
✔ Interpret approximate values between points

Students practise answering questions from time graphs by:
✔ Reading measurements accurately
✔ Calculating growth over time
✔ Estimating values from graph lines
✔ Identifying when measurements reach certain values

The lesson then introduces double time graphs.
Students learn that double time graphs compare two sets of data measured over the same period of time.

Students will:
✔ Compare two lines on one graph
✔ Read values from different datasets
✔ Calculate differences between lines
✔ Analyse changes over time visually

Next, students explore sponsored swim statistics.
They identify mistakes in bar charts and learn how incorrect data presentation can affect interpretation.

Students will also:
✔ Spot incorrect bar heights
✔ Compare chart data with frequency tables
✔ Correct graph errors
✔ Interpret swimming competition data
✔ Solve reasoning problems using bar charts

The lesson then introduces line graphs for journeys and distance over time.
Students learn that line graphs can be used to show continuous movement and changing measurements.

Students will:
✔ Estimate distances and times from line graphs
✔ Read approximate values
✔ Calculate time differences
✔ Interpret journeys visually

Finally, students investigate pets statistics.
They interpret bar charts and line graphs involving pet ownership, animal weights and kitten growth.

Students will also:
✔ Compare quantities from bar charts
✔ Calculate totals and differences
✔ Read decimal values from graphs
✔ Interpret weight graphs over time
✔ Estimate values between plotted points

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently interpret, compare and analyse data using bar charts, line graphs, time graphs and double time graphs.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Shapes 1
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students develop their understanding of angles and polygons. They learn how to identify, compare and order different types of angles and recognise angles within shapes.

Students begin by revising clockwise and anticlockwise turns.
They learn to identify quarter turns, half turns and three-quarter turns in different directions.

Students will:
✔ Identify clockwise and anticlockwise turns
✔ Recognise quarter, half and three-quarter turns
✔ Describe turns using correct mathematical language
✔ Find more than one way to reach the same position

The lesson then introduces angles as a measure of turn.
Students learn that an angle is formed between two straight lines and that a larger turn creates a larger angle.

Students will also:
✔ Understand angles as measures of turn
✔ Relate quarter turns to right angles
✔ Recognise that a full turn equals four right angles
✔ Identify right angles in different orientations

Next, students explore acute angles.
They learn that acute angles are smaller than a right angle.

Students will:
✔ Identify acute angles in different positions
✔ Compare acute angles
✔ Decide whether statements about acute angles are true or false
✔ Understand that acute angles can be different sizes

The lesson then introduces obtuse angles.
Students learn that obtuse angles are larger than a right angle but smaller than a half turn.

Students will also:
✔ Identify obtuse angles
✔ Compare obtuse and acute angles
✔ Use right-angle checkers to classify angles
✔ Explain reasoning using mathematical vocabulary

Students then investigate combinations of angles.
They learn that two acute angles can sometimes combine to make an obtuse angle, depending on their sizes.

Students will:
✔ Classify angles accurately
✔ Explain whether statements are always, sometimes or never true
✔ Compare different angle sizes
✔ Apply logical reasoning to angle problems

The lesson then explores polygons and interior angles.
Students learn that polygons are two-dimensional shapes with straight sides and that the angles inside them are called interior angles.

Students will also:
✔ Identify interior angles in polygons
✔ Count acute and obtuse angles within shapes
✔ Recognise different angle types in triangles, quadrilaterals and other polygons
✔ Correct misconceptions about polygon angles

Students then use a Venn diagram to classify polygons according to their interior angles.

They will:
✔ Sort polygons with acute angles
✔ Sort polygons with obtuse angles
✔ Identify polygons containing both acute and obtuse angles
✔ Compare different polygon properties

The lesson then focuses on comparing and ordering angles.
Students learn that the greater the turn, the greater the angle.

Students will also:
✔ Compare acute angles by size
✔ Compare obtuse angles by size
✔ Understand that larger acute angles are closer to a right angle
✔ Understand that larger obtuse angles are closer to a straight angle

Finally, students learn that the size of an angle depends on the amount of turn, not the length of the lines forming the angle.

Students will:
✔ Compare angles accurately regardless of line length
✔ Recognise equal angles in different drawings
✔ Explain why longer lines do not create larger angles
✔ Apply angle reasoning to solve comparison problems

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently identify, classify, compare and order acute, obtuse and right angles, and recognise how angles are used within polygons.
lessons.subject: maths

lessons.title: Shapes 2
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students develop their understanding of triangles and quadrilaterals. They learn how to identify, classify and compare different types of triangles and quadrilaterals using their properties.

Students begin by revising common polygons and identifying which shapes are triangles.
They learn that a triangle is a closed two-dimensional shape with three straight sides.

Students will:
✔ Identify common polygons
✔ Recognise triangles in different orientations
✔ Explain why some shapes are not triangles
✔ Use the properties of sides and vertices to classify shapes

The lesson then introduces different types of triangles.
Students learn how to identify equilateral, isosceles, scalene and right-angled triangles.

Students will also:
✔ Recognise equilateral triangles with three equal sides and three equal angles
✔ Identify isosceles triangles with two equal sides and two equal angles
✔ Identify scalene triangles with no equal sides
✔ Recognise right-angled triangles using the right-angle symbol
✔ Sort triangles according to their properties

Next, students explore perimeter problems involving triangles.
They use equal-side markings and known lengths to calculate missing sides and total perimeters.

Students will:
✔ Calculate the perimeter of equilateral triangles
✔ Calculate the perimeter of isosceles triangles
✔ Find missing side lengths using equal-side markings
✔ Use addition, subtraction and division to solve perimeter problems
✔ Apply reasoning skills to multi-step triangle questions

The lesson then uses clues to identify different triangle types.

Students will also:
✔ Match properties to triangle names
✔ Explain their reasoning using mathematical vocabulary
✔ Identify triangles from side and angle clues
✔ Compare different triangle classifications

The lesson then introduces parallel lines and quadrilaterals.
Students learn how to identify parallel sides and classify shapes according to their properties.

Students will:
✔ Identify pairs of parallel lines in polygons
✔ Understand that parallel lines never meet
✔ Recognise quadrilaterals as four-sided polygons
✔ Identify vertices and sides of quadrilaterals
✔ Distinguish between regular and irregular quadrilaterals

Students then compare different quadrilaterals.
They explore squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombuses, kites and trapeziums.

Students will also:
✔ Identify properties of squares and rectangles
✔ Compare parallelograms and rhombuses
✔ Recognise the properties of kites
✔ Identify trapeziums using parallel sides
✔ Understand which properties are shared between quadrilaterals

The lesson also develops reasoning skills using sorting and classification activities.

Students will:
✔ Sort quadrilaterals using properties such as right angles, equal sides and parallel sides
✔ Identify and correct classification mistakes
✔ Explain why shapes remain the same when rotated
✔ Use clues to identify quadrilaterals
✔ Apply mathematical vocabulary accurately

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently identify and classify triangles and quadrilaterals, calculate triangle perimeters, and use shape properties to solve reasoning and classification problems.

lessons.title: Shapes 3
lessons.description:
In this lesson, students develop their understanding of regular polygons, lines of symmetry and reflective symmetry. They learn how to identify symmetrical shapes, count lines of symmetry and complete symmetrical figures accurately.

Students begin by exploring regular and irregular polygons.
They learn that regular polygons have sides of equal length and angles of equal size.

Students will:
✔ Identify regular and irregular polygons
✔ Recognise pentagons, hexagons, heptagons and octagons
✔ Classify polygons by the number of sides
✔ Explain the difference between regular and irregular shapes

The lesson then explores perimeter in regular polygons.
Students learn that knowing the length of one side is enough to calculate the perimeter of a regular polygon.

Students will also:
✔ Calculate perimeters using multiplication
✔ Use equal side lengths to solve perimeter problems
✔ Apply division to find side lengths from known perimeters
✔ Solve reasoning problems involving regular polygons

Next, students investigate how perimeter and side length are connected.
They explore which regular polygons can be created from a fixed length of ribbon.

Students will:
✔ Divide perimeters into equal side lengths
✔ Identify when side lengths are whole numbers
✔ Compare different regular polygons
✔ Use multiplication and division to justify answers

The lesson then introduces lines of symmetry.
Students learn that a line of symmetry divides a shape into two matching mirror-image halves.

Students will also:
✔ Identify vertical, horizontal and diagonal lines of symmetry
✔ Use mirrors to test symmetry
✔ Explain why some lines are not lines of symmetry
✔ Recognise symmetry in different orientations

Students then explore lines of symmetry in common shapes.

Students will:
✔ Identify lines of symmetry in squares, rectangles and triangles
✔ Recognise shapes with no lines of symmetry
✔ Understand that circles have infinitely many lines of symmetry
✔ Compare the symmetry of different polygons

The lesson also investigates symmetry in regular polygons.
Students discover patterns between the number of sides and the number of lines of symmetry.

Students will:
✔ Count lines of symmetry in regular polygons
✔ Identify patterns in regular shapes
✔ Compare polygons with the most and fewest lines of symmetry
✔ Explain mathematical relationships using evidence

Next, students explore symmetrical figures.
They learn how lines of symmetry create matching mirror-image halves.

Students will also:
✔ Identify lines of symmetry in everyday objects and images
✔ Recognise symmetrical figures in different orientations
✔ Explain why figures are symmetrical
✔ Compare different types of symmetry

The lesson then develops reflection skills using grids.
Students learn how to reflect patterns accurately across mirror lines.

Students will:
✔ Reflect shaded squares across vertical and horizontal mirror lines
✔ Measure distances from the mirror line
✔ Complete symmetrical patterns
✔ Check reflections for accuracy

Students then apply reflection techniques to polygons.

They will:
✔ Identify and reflect vertices accurately
✔ Construct reflected polygons using grid coordinates
✔ Complete dissected symmetrical polygons
✔ Identify the polygons formed after reflection
✔ Solve reasoning problems involving vertices and symmetry

Finally, students explore reflections across more than one line of symmetry.
They learn how repeated reflections create fully symmetrical patterns.

Students will:
✔ Reflect shapes across multiple mirror lines
✔ Complete symmetrical designs in all directions
✔ Check that reflected points remain equal distances from mirror lines
✔ Apply symmetry skills to increasingly complex figures

By the end of the lesson, learners will confidently identify regular polygons, calculate their perimeters, recognise and count lines of symmetry, and complete symmetrical patterns and reflected shapes accurately.
